hyperedges.label: Project Case Study Pipeline (Content Model to Page)

nodes.label: mimo.xiaomi.com Primary Inspiration
nodes.rationale: Reference used only as direction for pacing, visual storytelling, premium presentation and motion quality; its visual assets, copywriting, branding, layout and proprietary implementation must not be copied.

nodes.label: Primary Stack
nodes.rationale: No dependency may be added unless the existing stack cannot reasonably solve the problem.

nodes.label: React (Interaction Islands Only)
nodes.rationale: React is allowed only for interaction-heavy islands; the site must not become a client-rendered React app.

nodes.label: ScrollTrigger Rules
nodes.rationale: ScrollTrigger is used only when scroll position meaningfully controls animation; avoid pinning overload, long pinned mobile sections and scroll-jacking.

nodes.label: Animation Principles
nodes.rationale: Animation is product experience, not decoration; every animation needs intentional purpose; prefer transform/opacity, avoid layout-heavy properties during scroll.

nodes.label: Motion Philosophy
nodes.rationale: The site feels smooth because motion is coherent, not because every element moves; motion must communicate hierarchy, continuity, spatial relationships, focus, transition and context - cinematic clarity, not visual noise.

nodes.label: Astro Framework Choice
nodes.rationale: Astro chosen for excellent fit with content-driven websites, static rendering, selective client-side interactivity via component islands, and lightweight default pages.

nodes.label: Accessibility Rules
nodes.rationale: Keyboard navigation, screen readers, focus states, contrast and reduced-motion support are required; animation must never block access to content.

nodes.label: Content Principles
nodes.rationale: Content must be concise, specific and believable; never invent employers, metrics, awards, testimonials or outcomes; projects presented as case studies, not cards.

nodes.label: Content Philosophy (Evidence over Claims)
nodes.rationale: The site communicates capability through evidence, not exaggerated claims; writing must be clear, specific, concise and human, avoiding buzzwords and AI-sounding filler.

nodes.label: Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Premium, modern, editorial, minimal but expressive, typography-led, motion-aware; explicitly avoids generated-template trends (glassmorphism, random gradients, SaaS aesthetics, generic AI layouts).

nodes.label: Design Philosophy (Premium, Restrained, Editorial)
nodes.rationale: Visual contrast comes from scale, spacing, typography, cropping and movement before decorative effects; the design must be recognizable through composition, not trendy effects.

nodes.label: Performance Rules
nodes.rationale: Site must stay fast despite rich motion: static Astro rendering, minimal client JS, islands only where necessary, lazy loading, no long-running timers on hidden pages.

nodes.label: Five-Act Storytelling Model
nodes.rationale: The homepage behaves as a narrative (Identity, Direction, Proof, Depth, Invitation) rather than a scanned document.

nodes.label: Positioning (IS Student + Creative Technologist + Product Builder)
nodes.norm_label: positioning (is student + creative technologist + product builder)

nodes.label: Documentation Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Decision priority order AGENTS > VISION > DESIGN > ANIMATION > ARCHITECTURE > COMPONENTS > CONTENT; on conflict the more specific rule must not contradict the project vision.

nodes.label: Portfolio Project Identity
nodes.rationale: The site must feel like a premium digital experience with visual storytelling, editorial composition, deliberate motion and high-quality interaction design - not a conventional resume or generic developer portfolio.

nodes.label: Data and UI Separation
nodes.rationale: Project content is data-driven: project data flows through case study components into the project page, so a page never duplicates its entire markup per project.

nodes.label: Project Content Collections
nodes.rationale: Project data is separated from page layout with schema validation, stable slugs and required fields so pages do not duplicate markup per project.

nodes.label: Placeholder Policy ([REPLACE:] Markers)
nodes.rationale: Explicit [REPLACE:] placeholders are used while content is unfinished so fake sample metrics never ship to production.

nodes.label: Hero Philosophy
nodes.rationale: The hero must not be the standard 'Hello, I am [Name]' template; it should immediately establish a visual world and a point of view through large display typography, a precise statement and choreographed entrance motion.

nodes.label: Project Philosophy (Curated Proof)
nodes.rationale: Selected work is the proof section; the homepage curates a small number of strong examples rather than presenting every project equally.

nodes.label: Animation Architecture (src/lib/animations)
nodes.rationale: Reusable motion logic is centralized in src/lib/animations (reveal.ts, hero.ts, parallax.ts, cursor.ts) instead of living in random component markup.

nodes.label: Animation Ownership Rule
nodes.rationale: A component owns animation only when it belongs to that component's behavior; global or cross-page animation lives in shared motion utilities so the same GSAP setup is never duplicated across project cards.

nodes.label: Responsive Rules
nodes.rationale: Mobile-first; mobile is not a shrunk desktop layout - it gets simplified choreography, reduced parallax and alternate composition.
